role: Author source-reading supplement; not an independent scientific review

claims.claim: The native source is Paenibacillus sp. JJ-1b, ATCC 35889. PraB/C/D were expressed in E. coli BL21(DE3); this host is an experimental preparation, not another native pathway taxon.
claims.source_locator: Table 1 (t1), JJ-1b and BL21(DE3) rows; sec6; sec18
claims.limitations: The 16S-based renamed strain label does not establish species-level Paenibacillus validus identity.

claims.claim: PraB was expressed from pETB23: pET21a(+) carrying a 1.9-kb NdeI–HindIII praB fragment. BL21(DE3) cells were induced with 1 mM IPTG at 30°C for 4 h.
claims.limitations: Table S1 primers were not obtained. Exact assay protein termini, additional residues and tag status are unresolved; native translation equality is not construct-sequence proof.

claims.claim: PraC was expressed from pETC23: pET21a(+) carrying a 0.4-kb NdeI–EcoRI praC fragment. BL21(DE3) cells were induced with 1 mM IPTG at 30°C for 4 h.
claims.limitations: Exact assay termini and tag status are unresolved without the primer/construct supplement. Do not infer native processed N-terminal proline from activity alone.

claims.claim: PraD was expressed from pC4D23: pColdIV carrying a 0.8-kb NdeI–XhoI praD fragment. BL21(DE3) cultures were cooled to 15°C and induced with 0.1 mM IPTG for 24 h.
claims.limitations: Exact assay termini and tag status are unresolved. These conditions differ from the pET21a(+) PraB/C preparations.

claims.claim: Sonicated cells were centrifuged at 15,000 × g for 15 min; supernatants were used as crude enzyme preparations. Reported PraB rates are per milligram of extract protein, not purified-enzyme turnover numbers.
claims.source_locator: sec6, last two sentences; sec9; sec22
claims.limitations: The main paper reports SDS-PAGE apparent masses of 58, 6 and 31 kDa for PraB/C/D. Supplementary Fig. S1 was not directly inspected; these are not native oligomer masses.

claims.claim: Crude PraB consumes HMS with NAD+ and yields an HMA-assigned product, supported by a 375-to-295-nm spectral change and a reported GC-MS derivative consistent with HMA.
claims.limitations: The original Fig. 3B raster was inspected. Supplementary GC-MS Fig. S3 was not obtained; its result is available only as the main paper’s report. This is not an independent E/Z assignment.

claims.claim: Crude PraB activity was 1.19 ± 0.07 U/mg with NAD+ and 0.113 ± 0.009 U/mg with NADP+. NAD+ is preferred by about 11-fold under these conditions; NADP+ also supports measurable activity.
claims.limitations: The specific-activity assay used 500 µM NAD(P)+, 50 µM HMS, pyruvate and lactate dehydrogenase at pH 7.3 and 35°C. The rates do not establish physiological coenzyme exclusivity.

numeric_scope.reported_error_type: not identified in the rate paragraph

claims.claim: Adding crude PraC during the PraB reaction shifts the product spectrum toward 236 nm, supporting HMA-to-OCA tautomerization. Figure 3C displays the rise near 236 nm with loss of the HMS signal.
claims.limitations: This is a coupled crude-extract spectral assay, not isolation of a stereochemically resolved product or proof of a particular tautomerase oligomer, catalytic residue or obligatory metal.

claims.claim: After crude PraD was added to the PraC mixture, an HPD-assigned HPLC peak appeared at 6.03 min after 10 min. Its spectrum peaked at 272 nm; initial OCA/HMA peaks were at 0.89/2.50 min.
claims.limitations: Identification rests on chromatography and spectral correspondence, including the historical 272-nm signature at pH 2.0. No authentic stereoisomer standard or independent exact E/Z assignment is reported here.

claims.claim: The PraD assay included 500 µM MgSO4, pH 7.3 Tris buffer and incubation at 35°C. Added magnesium is an explicit experimental condition.
claims.limitations: No magnesium omission, rescue, metal stoichiometry or physiological requirement experiment is reported for PraD in the inspected main paper. Do not turn this condition into a proven obligatory cofactor.

claims.claim: PraD activity was measured using its separately expressed crude extract added to a PraA/PraB/PraC-derived mixture; a PraE expression product was not a specified component of this assay.
claims.source_locator: sec5–sec6; sec11; sec22; Table 1, pC4D23 row
claims.limitations: This supports activity under that recombinant assay. It does not determine native assembly, subunit stoichiometry, absence of host contributions, or universal independence from hydratases.

claims.claim: The source distinguishes HMA, keto OCA and enol HPD. Figure 1 draws their proposed structures, while Figure 4 resolves a starting OCA/HMA mixture and the later HPD-assigned product.
claims.limitations: Historical names and schematic bond drawings are not independent modern stereochemical measurements. Do not use this paper alone to choose a disputed ChEBI/Rhea stereoisomer or substitute a keto tautomer for enol HPD.

claims.claim: PraE is assigned HPD hydratase by sequence similarity (52% identity to BphH; 45% to NbaH), with whole-cluster growth and cotranscription supporting its placement downstream of PraD.
claims.source_locator: Table 2 (t2), praE rows; sec24–sec25; sec27, PraE/F/G paragraph; Fig. 1A
claims.limitations: No individual PraE activity assay is reported in the inspected main text. Do not transfer another enzyme’s catalytic mechanism, stereospecificity, oligomer or cofactor requirements.

claims.claim: PraF is assigned HOV aldolase by sequence similarity (58% identity to NahM; 51% to XylK), with whole-cluster growth and cotranscription supporting the downstream role.
claims.source_locator: Table 2 (t2), praF rows; sec24–sec25; sec27, PraE/F/G paragraph; Fig. 1A
claims.limitations: No individual PraF activity, exact substrate stereoselectivity, metal effect or native assembly measurement is reported in the inspected main text.

claims.claim: PraG is assigned the acetaldehyde-to-acetyl-CoA step by sequence similarity (61% identity to NahO; 53% to NbaJ), with whole-cluster growth and cotranscription providing pathway-context support.
claims.source_locator: Table 2 (t2), praG rows; sec24–sec25; sec27, PraE/F/G paragraph; Fig. 1A
claims.limitations: No individual PraG acetaldehyde, CoA or coenzyme assay is reported in the inspected main text. Endpoint chemistry and physiological coenzyme specificity are not separately measured here.

claims.claim: E. coli BL21(DE3) carrying pBRI23 with praR-praABEGFDCHI acquired growth on M9 medium containing 10 mM 4HB as sole carbon source within 10 days. This supports a functional transferred 4HB catabolic gene set.
claims.limitations: Supplementary Fig. S4 was not inspected. The result is not a separate biochemical assay of PraE/F/G, a measured product balance, or evidence that native JJ-1b executes the entire catechol-initiated route.

claims.claim: RT-PCR supports one praABEGFDCHI transcriptional unit and separate praR transcription. Catabolic transcripts were evident after JJ-1b growth on 4HB or PCA and not evident under the reported succinate condition.
claims.limitations: All three gel panels were visually inspected. This evidence concerns transcription, not subcellular localization, a protein complex or direct catalytic flux.

claims.claim: In E. coli DH5α, a praR-containing praA promoter–lacZ reporter increased activity with 4HB or PCA, while the reporter lacking praR was constitutively active. The result supports PraR-dependent repression.
claims.limitations: Figure 7, not Figure 8, is the reporter experiment. It does not establish direct ligand binding, direct DNA occupancy or inhibition of whole-pathway metabolic flux; reporter DNA identity must remain explicit.

claims.claim: PraA first generates the 350-nm 5CHMS-assigned species, which shifts toward HMS over a longer incubation. PraH accelerates the 350-to-375-nm conversion on the short assay timescale.
claims.limitations: Failure to recover 5CHMS after extraction/GC-MS does not establish direct PraA production of HMS. Decarboxylation during preparation or analysis is explicitly considered by the authors.

claims.claim: The experimentally reconstructed entry is 4HB→PCA→5CHMS→HMS, sharing PraB/C/D and inferred PraE/F/G chemistry with a catechol meta-cleavage tail. The study does not establish a catechol ring-cleavage enzyme in JJ-1b.
claims.limitations: Represent component evidence without promoting native JJ-1b to experimentally demonstrated whole MetaCyc:PWY-5420 scope. This is a bounded assessment of this main article, not a species-wide absence claim.

claims.claim: Figure 8 compares pra with xyl, nah and dmp clusters and with predicted clusters in other bacilli. A proposed benzoate transporter appears in the B. licheniformis comparison.
claims.limitations: Comparative synteny does not prove JJ-1b transport, exact protein activity, compartment or a whole route in the comparison taxa. The missing hydrolase is scoped to the sequenced pra cluster.

claims.claim: The main study supplies no PraB/C/D native oligomer determination or direct catalytic-residue experiment. Homolog identities in Table 2 and automatic sequence annotations must retain their inferential status.
claims.limitations: Do not transfer XylG dimer, XylH hexamer, decarboxylase–hydratase complex or specific residue chemistry to PraB/C/D as measured in this paper. Main-paper absence is bounded; supplementary contents remain unread.

claims.claim: Figure 4 is the PraD HPLC product experiment. Figure 5 instead shows PraI conversion of 4HB to PCA; Figure 7 is the PraR reporter and Figure 8 is comparative gene organization.
claims.source_locator: Fig. 4–5 and Fig. 7–8, original rasters and captions
claims.limitations: Keep these evidence locations distinct when adapting predecessor claims.
